Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address City Council, please complete a speaker card and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public
comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote and on matters not listed on the
agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council: Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less
and
directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are
available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the
agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has
been posted will also be made available for public inspection. Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City
Clerk’s Department, during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every
other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

Councilmember Valencia congratulated Norma Amescua, as the incoming President of
the Norwalk Lions Club of California; reported on her attendance at the Summer
Concert/National Night Out, Norwalk Transit 50th Anniversary, Southeast Water Coalition
Board of Directors Meeting, Milagro Cinemas Grand Opening, Los Angeles Care Health
Plan “Back-to-School Resource Fair,” and the Milagro Cinemas Commendation

Beyond the Classroom event will be held August 10; wished all students, teachers, and
staff a happy school year. Councilmember Perez congratulated Jim Parker, Executive
Director of Regional Transportation, on 50 years of success within the Transportation
Department; shared that City newsletters and bulletins were distributed; reported on her
attendance at the Peace Officers Association of Los Angeles County meeting, the
California Joint Powers Insurance Authority Annual Board of Directors meeting, briefing
with Los Angeles County Sheriff Luna, Board of Supervisors weekly meeting, and
California Contract Cities Executive Board Planning Session; and invited all to attend the
Summer Concert and Norwalk Chamber of Commerce Annual “Business Expo” August 7.
Councilmember Ramirez reported on his attendance at the Los Angeles County
Sanitation District meeting, the Firestone Widening Groundbreaking Ceremony, and the
City of Santa Fe Springs’ Renovated Aquatics Center Opening. Vice Mayor Ayala
recognized members of the audience, thanked the Homeless Operation Prevention and
Engagement and Public Safety for their hard work; announced the upcoming Senior
Center Lobby Olympics being held August 7 and 9. Mayor Rios reported on her
attendance at the Milagro Cinemas Grand Opening, Public Safety Neighborhood Watch
meeting, Firestone Widening Groundbreaking Ceremony, Norwalk Santa Fe Springs

International Brands, Inc. (Kimball) via Omnia Partners’ solicitation titled “Request for Proposal

Transit Facility Tenant Improvement Project No. 7865. The furniture replaces existing furniture
that has reached its useful life in the tenant improvement area in Transit Operations, Dispatch,
Vehicle Maintenance and Transit Administration.

services jointly with other recipients or participate in purchasing cooperatives to obtain better
pricing through larger purchases.

adopted budget. There is no impact to the general fund.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION NO. 24-44 - BUDGET AMENDMENT FOR PURCHASE OF
  UTILITY TRUCK FOR NORWALK TRANSIT SYSTEM

Background:

On February 15, 2024, the City issued Invitation for Bid (IFB) No. 24-738 for a Class 4 Medium
Duty Utility Truck. The purpose of the IFB is to acquire a new shop truck to replace the current
shop truck for the Equipment Maintenance division. The current shop truck is 24 years old and
needs costly major repairs. The new shop truck will be utilized for roadcalls and field repairs for
City-Wide vehicles and Norwalk Transit System (NTS) fleet.

NTS received one bid from BP Ford of Long Beach for a 2024 Ford F450 Super-Duty Cab &
Chassis truck. When a single bid is received in response to this IFB, NTS staff has to determine
if the quality of service meets or exceeds the department’s expectations, and if the price is fair
and reasonable. The Manufacturer Suggested Retail Price for this vehicle starts at $68,690. The
custom utility body ranges from $50,000 and up depending on the customized features. Based
on these findings, the bid price of $148,731 including tax and license fees submitted by BP Ford
of Long Beach is fair and reasonable. Also, the vehicle meets or exceeds the department’s
expectations.

Fiscal Impact:

Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-44, authorizing the use of Transit
Reserves and a budget amendment to the Fiscal Year 2024/25 Department of Transportation
Capital Budget in the amount of $148,731 There is no impact to the general fund.

Service (SMS) Engagement Platform (Ascendant). This platform will serve as a critical tool for
disseminating important information, facilitating two-way communication, and improving overall
civic engagement.

In 2023, the City piloted the use of Ascendant to promote events at a local level. In one of the
Movie Nights at the Park events, Ascendant notified neighborhoods around the event site. This
resulted in a 22% increase in attendance compared to the previous year.

The implementation of Ascendant offers the community the following benefits:

  1. Enhanced Communication: The platform will enable the City to send timely updates and
  alerts directly to residents' mobile devices, ensuring critical information is received
  promptly.
  2. Increased Civic Engagement: By facilitating two-way communication, residents can
  provide feedback and engage in meaningful dialogue with the City, fostering a more
  involved and informed community.
  3. Emergency Notifications: The ability to quickly disseminate emergency notifications will
  enhance public safety and preparedness. This feature will supplement the City’s RAVE
  emergency notification system, if needed.
  4. Cost-Effective Solution: The comprehensive service package offered by Ascendant
  provides a cost-effective solution for modernizing the city's communication infrastructure.

SUBJECT:  MUNICIPAL LAW ENFORCEMENT SERVICES AGREEMENT RENEWAL

Background:

The current Municipal Law Enforcement Services Agreement (MLESA) between Norwalk and
the County of Los Angeles (LACO) expired on June 30, 2024. A five-year agreement between
the City and LACO has been prepared for City Council’s review and approval. The term of the
contract will commence on July 1, 2024, and expire on June 30, 2029.

The rates for law enforcement services are provided by the County of Los Angeles Auditor-
Controller on an annual basis. Rates are determined based on the fully burdened cost of
deploying patrol units including variables such as salary, benefits, equipment (vehicles, radios,
maintenance, etc.), management overhead, vacation and sick relief, Detective services,
Dispatch and front desk personnel, station Jailer services and civilian positions.

This year, a subcommittee of California Contract Cities Association (CCCA) City Managers was
formed to draft revisions to the MLESA. Comments were solicited from all contract cities.

The CCCA subcommittee worked closely with the Sheriff’s Department Contract Law
Enforcement Bureau to develop new language in the MLESA to describe how resource
deployment will be addressed.

The following list summarizes the changes to the MESLA for 2024-2029:
  • Section 3.3 – The following language was added to address deployment deficiencies,
  accurately track contract minutes on a monthly basis and by service type, rather than the
  current method of compiling all contract minutes into just one bucket of total contract
  minutes, while still maintaining 98% service compliance.

  service unit type, then the Sheriff's Department Station Captain shall meet with the
